transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I keep messing up little things. Just... careless stuff. Like, I'll write the wrong time down on a class sheet over at the senior center. Or... I'll measure a board for a project and still end up cutting it a hair short, just because I skipped over the small print. Just... things like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
No. Not really. I mean... I feel fine, mostly. Just... not depressed.
Do you worry a lot most days?
No. Not really. I mean... just the usual stuff, I guess. But no, I wouldn't say I worry a lot.
Did these kinds of careless mistakes start when you were a child?

Yeah. I suppose so. Um... even back in elementary school, my teachers would write that I was bright, but... I was always forgetting my books. Or losing my homework. I'd just... stare out the window, mostly. Unless someone kept me on track.
Do these attention and careless mistakes cause problems for you in more than one part of your life, like at work, home, or in school?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. Um... it comes up in a few places. Like, I used to help run these DIY workshops, but I stepped back because of the mix-ups. And at home... my wife usually has to double-check our plans now. Just so I don't mess up the times for family visits or stuff at the community center.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a longstanding pattern of inattention beginning in childhood with careless mistakes, losing/forgetting school materials, drifting off/staring out the window, and needing external prompting to stay on track. Symptoms cause impairment in multiple settings (work/volunteering and home). This is most consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation.
